newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE sees sheep meat prices off, output up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE sees sheep meat prices off, output up.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said it expects average saleyard prices for Australian lamb and mutton to ease slightly in 1996/97 in response to an expansion in supplies and increased competition from beef.

Mutton prices were forecast to fall by 5.8 percent to average A$0.60 per kg in 1996/97, while lamb prices were seen off 2.5 percent to A$1.96 per kg, ABARE said in its quarterly Commodities publication, released on Tuesday.
Exports of both mutton and lamb were forecast to rise, but exports of live sheep should dip slightly, ABARE said.

"Lamb and mutton exports from Australia are forecast to increase in 1996/97 by 9.6 percent and 2.8 percent respectively, reflecting the increased export supply availability caused by higher domestic production and relatively stable domestic consumption," the agency said.
Live sheep exports were expected to fall 1.8 percent by volume due to a shortage of suitable adult sheep, but the total value of exports was expected to rise marginally, ABARE said.
"The stronger demand from Middle East markets, together with tighter Australian supply, is forecast to result in some bidding up of prices for live sheep exports," said ABARE.

The shortage of lamb in the U.S., the largest market for Australian lamb, was expected to ease only moderately in 1996/97 so Australian exports to this destination were expected to expand, the forecaster added.

Australian lamb production was expected to rise by 4.6 percent to 272,000 tonnes reflecting a sharp rise in slaughtering, while mutton output was forecast to rise 3.4 percent to 305,000 tonnes in response to a continued shift out of wool production, ABARE said.
